findings.issue_text: Legacy writes in dualwriter_mode3.go run in background goroutines with context derived from the incoming request ctx, so when the API request completes the context cancellation aborts the in-flight legacy write
Legacy write errors are only fed into metrics (recordLegacyDuration) and never logged or propagated, causing silent divergence between unified and legacy storage

Update's legacy goroutine calls d.Legacy.Update without the updateWrapper, so legacy storage re-evaluates objInfo.UpdatedObject against legacy's old object which may differ, causing stores to end up with different contents
Create records storage errors via recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration, mislabeling storage failures as legacy failures
Update records storage errors via recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration, mislabeling storage failures as legacy failures
Delete success path records metrics with 'name' instead of options.Kind as the label, making delete durations unqueryable/aggregated incorrectly
DeleteCollection goroutine records legacy duration via recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration

Create passes the storage-created object (with unified-store resourceVersion) into legacy Create, so a legacy failure is invisible and mode 3 can report success while the object exists only in unified storage, breaking rollback/downgrade paths
Delete builds log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", ...) but then overwrites with klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log), discarding name/kind from context-derived logs
Get/List/Update read options.Kind for metrics, but these client-supplied options are typically empty, causing metric series to collapse into an unlabeled bucket

Delete behavior change: new code returns immediately on any unified error including NotFound, skipping legacy cleanup, so objects left only in legacy storage during a mode transition will fail to delete

Legacy writes in dualwriter_mode3.go (Create, Delete, Update, DeleteCollection) are fire-and-forget goroutines with errors only logged/metered, so legacy failures are invisible and the two stores silently diverge with no retry or outbox (data loss)

Goroutines in dualwriter_mode3.go derive context from the request context, which is cancelled when the handler returns, aborting legacy writes with context.Canceled before the 10s timeout; timeout should use context.Background()/detached values

Data race in dualwriter_mode3.go Create: the background legacy-write goroutine uses the same runtime.Object returned to the HTTP layer without a deep copy, so the apiserver may serialize/mutate it concurrently with the legacy store reading it (same shape in Update via objInfo callbacks)

Update in dualwriter_mode3.go passes the original objInfo to d.Legacy.Update instead of the updateWrapper wrapping the unified-storage-written object, so legacy re-runs UpdatedObject against its own old object and may write a different object than unified, causing divergence

Metrics mislabeled: in Update the storage failure path calls recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage) instead of recordStorageDuration, and in DeleteCollection the legacy duration is recorded via recordStorageDuration, giving wrong dashboards
Unbounded goroutine fan-out per write request in dualwriter_mode3.go with no concurrency cap, queue, or backpressure; slow legacy store causes goroutines and pinned object payloads to accumulate

Fire-and-forget goroutines for legacy writes silently lose failed writes with no logging, retry, or reconciliation, and process shutdown can kill them mid-flight, causing data divergence between stores
Legacy write goroutines lack panic recovery, so a panic in the legacy store takes down the whole process

Legacy write goroutines derive their timeout context from the request context, which is canceled after the handler returns, so legacy writes can be canceled before starting; should derive from context.Background()
Delete returns early on any storage error from unified store including NotFound, skipping the legacy delete and leaving orphaned objects in legacy storage
Update goroutine passes the raw objInfo to legacy store instead of the object stored in unified, causing UpdatedObject to run against the legacy object and produce divergent results
Running objInfo concurrently with the request's callback is unsafe if the callback touches request-scoped state

Wrong metric recorded on storage failures: Update and Create error paths call recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, and DeleteCollection calls recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, corrupting migration health signals
Delete success path records `name` instead of kind as metric label, causing high-cardinality object names and breaking aggregation
Delete discards the enriched logger by setting ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of log, losing name/kind/method values in telemetry
Create returns `created, err` where err is provably nil after the early error return
No concurrency bound or backpressure on legacy write goroutines; unbounded goroutines under burst load can pile up for up to 10s each, delaying GC and potentially OOMing

TestMode3_Delete and TestMode3_DeleteCollection set only the storage mock, so the async goroutine calling Legacy.Delete/DeleteCollection panics on unset mock expectations, crashing the test binary non-deterministically
TestMode3_Create error case mocks only legacy storage (setupStorageFn is nil) but Create calls Storage.Create first, so the error path doesn't exercise the intended failure
Mode 3 tests lack AssertExpectations and legacy-call-count assertions, so nothing verifies the async legacy write (the core dual-write contract) actually happens

Update now passes raw objInfo to legacy instead of the updateWrapper with the storage-returned object, so legacy may persist different content/resourceVersion than unified storage, with no test covering this divergence
Async legacy writes derive from the request ctx which may be cancelled when the handler returns; no test covers context cancellation, the 10s timeout path, or swallowed legacy-write errors

Metrics are misattributed: Create/Update error paths record storage duration as legacy metric, and DeleteCollection async legacy path calls recordStorageDuration for the legacy call; no metrics-assertion test exists
wantErr test cases only assert.Error and return early without asserting which store produced the error or calling AssertExpectations, so error paths may pass for spurious reasons

TestMode3_Delete error case returns before async legacy goroutine can run, risking cross-test contamination via the now-shared package-level prometheus registry (mode1 test removed its local registry), which can panic on duplicate metric registration

Silent fire-and-forget divergence from legacy storage: legacy writes converted to untracked goroutines with 10s timeout; failures cause permanent divergence with no retry, queue, or error surfacing beyond a metric (dualwriter_mode3.go Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection)
Update no longer propagates the unified-store result to legacy: objInfo is passed raw to d.Legacy.Update so legacy re-derives from its own stale state; updateWrapper may now be dead code
Data race: obj, options, listOptions, and request-scoped ctx are handed to background goroutines while the handler continues; storage layers mutate passed objects
Delete regression: NotFound from unified store aborts and skips legacy delete, though old code tolerated NotFound and still deleted from legacy
Metric calls record the wrong backend: Create/Update error paths call recordLegacyDuration on storage failures; DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration for a legacy operation
Delete success metric passes name in the kind label slot, creating unbounded label cardinality and polluting per-kind aggregation
Duplication: legacy-goroutine boilerplate is copy-pasted 4x in Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection; should be extracted into a helper
Delete builds a detailed log with WithValues but discards it, using d.Log in klog.NewContext instead; error branch logs without name/kind

Tests are racy/nondeterministic against new async writes: tests assert immediately without waiting for goroutines, and unified-store failure test cases stub only legacy so unstubbed storage calls panic on mock.Mock
Test assertions are tautological: repeated assert.NotEqual(t, obj, anotherObj) lines assert nothing, and TestMode3_Create checks a fixture property (GetResourceVersion()=="1") not behavior
Create returns (created, err) after err was checked nil; misleading and will break silently if the guard above is edited
Mode 1 test change removes local prometheus registry and depends on shared package-level p, creating hidden cross-test coupling and potential registration races in concurrent subtests

Mode 3 semantics changed from synchronous legacy sync to best-effort divergent background sync with no reconciliation mechanism; needs an explicit divergence-handling strategy (retry queue, backfill job)

Legacy write goroutines in dualwriter_mode3.go use the incoming request context as parent, which is cancelled when the handler returns, so legacy writes are typically aborted immediately and the legacy store diverges; goroutines must use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a background context

Delete regresses NotFound handling: new code returns early on any unified storage error, so legacy-only objects (created before mode 3) fail to delete from unified and their legacy copy is orphaned forever; same pattern in DeleteCollection

Update's legacy goroutine passes the original objInfo to d.Legacy.Update, re-deriving the object from legacy's old state with non-deterministic UpdatedObject, causing the two stores to store different objects; also silently errors if legacy has no object and forceAllowCreate is false

Shared runtime.Object is used concurrently by unified Storage.Create (which mutates it with resourceVersion/UID/timestamps), the client response serialization, and the legacy goroutine, creating a data race
Delete success path records the user-controlled object name as a metric label instead of options.Kind, causing unbounded Prometheus label cardinality / registry bloat

Misattributed metrics: Create storage-error path calls recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration; Update storage-error path has the same swap; DeleteCollection legacy goroutine calls recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration
Legacy goroutine errors are silently swallowed with no retry, log, or count; error logging present in old code was removed in this diff, leaving no mechanism to detect or repair legacy misses
Delete builds a structured log with name/kind/method values but passes the base d.Log to klog.NewContext, so goroutine calls lose the structured log fields

Tests in dualwriter_mode3_test.go reference an undefined registry variable p (only declared in TestMode3_Get), so tests don't compile unless p is a package-level var elsewhere; also TestMode3_Update's async failure-path goroutine makes mock expectations non-deterministic
Tests never assert LegacyStorage.Create/Update/Delete were invoked, so mode 3's core dual-write contract is untested and tests pass even if legacy writes never happen
List/Get metrics use options.Kind as a label, but TypeMeta on options is typically empty from real clients, making the kind dimension near-always empty and useless for per-resource failure analysis

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy writes in dualwriter_mode3.go run in background goroutines with context derived from the incoming request ctx, so when the API request completes the context cancellation aborts the in-flight legacy write

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes are moved into background goroutines (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`) and those goroutines derive their context from the incoming request `ctx` via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`. Because the parent `ctx` is the request context, it will typically be canceled when the API request completes; that cancellation propagates to the derived context and can abort the in-flight legacy operation, causing the legacy write to be skipped/fail much more often than before (previously legacy writes were synchronous within the request).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy write errors are only fed into metrics (recordLegacyDuration) and never logged or propagated, causing silent divergence between unified and legacy storage

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3` the legacy writes are now executed asynchronously in goroutines for `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection`, and the goroutines only call `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)` with the error state; they never log the legacy error and they do not propagate it back to the caller (e.g., `Create` starts `go func(){ _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Create(...); d.recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, ...) }()` with no `log.Error`). Previously, legacy write failures were at least logged synchronously (e.g., old `Create`/`Update`/`Delete` code logged legacy errors). This change can therefore cause silent divergence between unified storage and legacy storage when the legacy operation fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update's legacy goroutine calls d.Legacy.Update without the updateWrapper, so legacy storage re-evaluates objInfo.UpdatedObject against legacy's old object which may differ, causing stores to end up with different contents

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the diff removed the prior logic that precomputed `updated := objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` and passed an `updateWrapper{updated: obj}` to legacy to ensure the same object content is written to both stores. The new code calls `d.Storage.Update(...)` and then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the original `objInfo` (no wrapper), so legacy will re-run `UpdatedObject` against legacy’s current/old object, which may differ from storage’s, leading to divergent persisted objects between stores.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Create records storage errors via recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration, mislabeling storage failures as legacy failures
matched_golden_ids: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: in DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection, a storage failure path uses recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, causing storage failures/durations to be mislabeled as legacy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update records storage errors via recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration, mislabeling storage failures as legacy failures

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go` within `(*DualWriterMode3).Update`, the error path after `d.Storage.Update(...)` calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. This is a storage failure being recorded via the legacy-duration metric function, which misattributes the error to the legacy side. The diff clearly shows `recordLegacyDuration` used with `startStorage` on the storage update error branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete success path records metrics with 'name' instead of options.Kind as the label, making delete durations unqueryable/aggregated incorrectly
DeleteCollection goroutine records legacy duration via recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go` within `DeleteCollection`, the async legacy write goroutine measures `startLegacy := time.Now()` and calls `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)`, but then records the duration with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`. This is a concrete, diff-verifiable mismatch that will misattribute legacy operation latency/error metrics as storage metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Create passes the storage-created object (with unified-store resourceVersion) into legacy Create, so a legacy failure is invisible and mode 3 can report success while the object exists only in unified storage, breaking rollback/downgrade paths

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the goroutine calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` with the original `obj`, not the `created` object returned from unified storage, so it does not pass the unified-store resourceVersion into legacy Create. Also, mode 3 already returned success even if legacy Create failed in the pre-diff code (it logged the error and returned `created, nil`), so the claimed rollback/downgrade break is not newly introduced by this diff as stated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete builds log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", ...) but then overwrites with klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log), discarding name/kind from context-derived logs
Get/List/Update read options.Kind for metrics, but these client-supplied options are typically empty, causing metric series to collapse into an unlabeled bucket

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3 the new logging/metrics labels use the `Kind` field from request option structs (e.g., `Get`: `d.Log.WithValues("kind", options.Kind, ...)` and `d.recordStorageDuration(..., options.Kind, ...)`; `List`: `options.Kind`; `Update`: `options.Kind`). These option objects are passed in from callers and the diff shows no fallback to a server-known kind/resource when `Kind` is empty, so metrics can end up labeled with an empty kind value (collapsing series). This affects observability/metrics cardinality rather than core request correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete behavior change: new code returns immediately on any unified error including NotFound, skipping legacy cleanup, so objects left only in legacy storage during a mode transition will fail to delete

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Delete() previously ignored unified-store NotFound (apierrors.IsNotFound) and still attempted Legacy.Delete, ensuring legacy-only objects could be cleaned up during transitions. The new implementation returns immediately on any storage error (`if err != nil { ... return res, async, err }`) and no longer special-cases NotFound, so legacy cleanup is skipped when the unified store reports NotFound, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy writes in dualwriter_mode3.go (Create, Delete, Update, DeleteCollection) are fire-and-forget goroutines with errors only logged/metered, so legacy failures are invisible and the two stores silently diverge with no retry or outbox (data loss)

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes for `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection` were changed from synchronous calls to `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.<op>(...) ... }()` (fire-and-forget). Those goroutines do not return errors to the caller and, in most cases, do not even log failures (they only call `recordLegacyDuration(...)` / metrics). This does make legacy-write failures effectively invisible to request handling and can allow the legacy store to fall out of sync with Storage without any in-band signal. However, whether that is a “bug” (vs. an intended best-effort legacy write in Mode3) is not provable solely from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Goroutines in dualwriter_mode3.go derive context from the request context, which is cancelled when the handler returns, aborting legacy writes with context.Canceled before the 10s timeout; timeout should use context.Background()/detached values

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes are dispatched asynchronously (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection start a `go func()` and then return), but inside each goroutine the timeout context is derived from the same `ctx` passed into the request handler: `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)`. Because the parent `ctx` may be canceled as soon as the request finishes, these background legacy writes can be aborted early with `context.Canceled` before the intended 10s timeout, undermining the best-effort legacy replication behavior implied by the async goroutine.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Data race in dualwriter_mode3.go Create: the background legacy-write goroutine uses the same runtime.Object returned to the HTTP layer without a deep copy, so the apiserver may serialize/mutate it concurrently with the legacy store reading it (same shape in Update via objInfo callbacks)

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the change introduces an async legacy write: `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...) }()` while the method returns `created` immediately. Although the goroutine uses `obj` (the input) rather than `created`, the diff provides no guarantee these are distinct—`d.Storage.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` can plausibly mutate and/or return the same underlying object pointer passed in. That would make the returned object potentially shared with the goroutine, risking concurrent reads/writes (serialization/caller use vs legacy store) with no deep copy or immutability guarantee. A similar async pattern is introduced in `Update` where the goroutine reuses `objInfo` after returning, which can also encapsulate mutable state/callback behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update in dualwriter_mode3.go passes the original objInfo to d.Legacy.Update instead of the updateWrapper wrapping the unified-storage-written object, so legacy re-runs UpdatedObject against its own old object and may write a different object than unified, causing divergence

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Update() now calls d.Storage.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...) and then (in a goroutine) calls d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...). The previous implementation wrapped objInfo in an updateWrapper containing the already-updated object so legacy would persist the same object that unified storage wrote. With the wrapper removed and the original objInfo reused, legacy can re-run UpdatedObject against its own “old” object and produce a different result, causing divergence between storages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metrics mislabeled: in Update the storage failure path calls recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage) instead of recordStorageDuration, and in DeleteCollection the legacy duration is recorded via recordStorageDuration, giving wrong dashboards

adjudication.rationale:
In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, metrics recording is incorrect in two places:
1) `Update`: after `startStorage := time.Now()`, the storage update error path calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` even though the timing is for the storage operation; it should record storage duration.
2) `DeleteCollection`: in the goroutine for the legacy delete-collection call, it records the legacy timing via `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`; this should use `recordLegacyDuration`.
These will mislabel metrics and skew dashboards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded goroutine fan-out per write request in dualwriter_mode3.go with no concurrency cap, queue, or backpressure; slow legacy store causes goroutines and pinned object payloads to accumulate

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy writes are launched in a new goroutine for each request (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection all use `go func() { ... d.Legacy.<op>(...) }()`), with only a per-goroutine 10s timeout and no global concurrency cap, queue, or backpressure. Under high write rate or slow/hung legacy storage, goroutines (capturing `obj`/args in the closure) can accumulate up to request_rate×timeout, risking memory/goroutine exhaustion and degraded availability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fire-and-forget goroutines for legacy writes silently lose failed writes with no logging, retry, or reconciliation, and process shutdown can kill them mid-flight, causing data divergence between stores

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes were changed from synchronous calls (with error logging) to fire-and-forget goroutines for `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, and `DeleteCollection` (e.g., `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create/... }()`). These goroutines do not log errors/timeouts (they only record metrics), and the request returns immediately after the unified-store operation. This makes legacy persistence non-deterministic (can be cut off on process shutdown or not complete before subsequent logic), and failures are effectively silent, which can cause divergence between Storage and LegacyStorage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy write goroutines lack panic recovery, so a panic in the legacy store takes down the whole process

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes are now executed in background goroutines (e.g., `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create(...) ... }()`, similarly for Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) without any `defer`/`recover`. In Go, an unrecovered panic in any goroutine will crash the entire process, so this change introduces an operational robustness risk for these async legacy writes. The diff doesn’t show whether legacy storage can panic, so it’s not provably a functional defect, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded concern created by the new goroutines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy write goroutines derive their timeout context from the request context, which is canceled after the handler returns, so legacy writes can be canceled before starting; should derive from context.Background()

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, the legacy write/delete/update calls are now run in goroutines and their timeout contexts are derived from the incoming ctx (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection use `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` inside `go func() { ... }`). This couples the background legacy operation lifetime to the caller/request context. The diff itself does not prove that ctx is always canceled immediately after the handler returns, but it does show the legacy work can be canceled early if the parent ctx is canceled, which is a significant behavioral concern for asynchronous writes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete returns early on any storage error from unified store including NotFound, skipping the legacy delete and leaving orphaned objects in legacy storage

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Delete() was changed to immediately return on any error from d.Storage.Delete ("if err != nil { ... return res, async, err }") and the legacy delete is only executed in a goroutine after a successful storage delete. The previous implementation explicitly ignored NotFound from storage (apierrors.IsNotFound) and still attempted legacy deletion. With the new code, a NotFound from unified storage will skip legacy deletion, potentially leaving legacy objects undeleted (orphaned).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update goroutine passes the raw objInfo to legacy store instead of the object stored in unified, causing UpdatedObject to run against the legacy object and produce divergent results

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the new implementation updates Unified Store first (`d.Storage.Update(...)`) and then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(...)` passing the original `objInfo` (`d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)`). The previous code explicitly computed the updated object from Unified Store and wrapped `objInfo` so Legacy used the already-updated object (`updateWrapper{updated: obj}`), preventing Legacy from recomputing `UpdatedObject` against its own (potentially different) “old” object. With the wrapper removed, Legacy may re-run `UpdatedObject` against Legacy state and diverge from what was written to Unified Store.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Running objInfo concurrently with the request's callback is unsafe if the callback touches request-scoped state

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the PR changes legacy writes to run asynchronously in a goroutine and passes the same `objInfo` into `d.Legacy.Update(...)` after `d.Storage.Update(...)` has completed and the handler may be returning (`go func() { ... d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...) }()`). Since `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` is effectively a callback into request-supplied logic, using it asynchronously (potentially after the request is done/canceled) can be unsafe if it captures request-scoped state or isn’t safe to invoke outside the request lifecycle. The diff shows the async invocation; the actual unsafety depends on the concrete `objInfo` implementation, which isn’t shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Wrong metric recorded on storage failures: Update and Create error paths call recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration, and DeleteCollection calls recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, corrupting migration health signals

adjudication.rationale:
In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, several metric recordings are clearly swapped/mismatched:
- Create(): after Storage.Create fails, it calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage) even though the failure was in Storage (should be recordStorageDuration).
- Update(): after Storage.Update fails, it calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage) even though the failure was in Storage.
- DeleteCollection(): in the goroutine that invokes d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, it records with d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy) even though this measures the legacy operation (should be recordLegacyDuration).
These are verifiable from the diff and would corrupt the intended storage-vs-legacy duration/error signals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete success path records `name` instead of kind as metric label, causing high-cardinality object names and breaking aggregation
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that metrics labeling uses the object `name` instead of the resource kind (`options.Kind`), creating inconsistency with other methods and harming aggregation/high-cardinality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete discards the enriched logger by setting ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of log, losing name/kind/method values in telemetry

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Delete() builds an enriched logger `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then sets the context with `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`. As a result, downstream calls like `d.Storage.Delete(ctx, ...)` and the goroutine legacy delete will not receive the enriched logger via context (only the base `d.Log`), so name/kind/method values are lost from context-based logging/telemetry. This is a real, diff-grounded issue but primarily affects observability rather than functional correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Create returns `created, err` where err is provably nil after the early error return

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, after `created, err := d.Storage.Create(...)`, the function early-returns on `err != nil`. If it continues, `err` is necessarily `nil`, so `return created, err` is equivalent to `return created, nil`. That’s not a correctness defect; at most it’s a minor readability nit, not a verifiable bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No concurrency bound or backpressure on legacy write goroutines; unbounded goroutines under burst load can pile up for up to 10s each, delaying GC and potentially OOMing

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy operations are now dispatched in fire-and-forget goroutines (`go func() { ... }()`) in multiple methods: `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection`. Each request spawns a new goroutine with a 10s timeout (`context.WithTimeoutCause(..., time.Second*10, ...)`) but there is no semaphore/worker pool/backpressure to bound concurrent legacy writes. Under burst load, these goroutines can accumulate for up to ~10s each, increasing memory/GC pressure and potentially leading to resource exhaustion. This is a concrete, diff-grounded scalability/operational concern rather than an immediate functional correctness failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestMode3_Delete and TestMode3_DeleteCollection set only the storage mock, so the async goroutine calling Legacy.Delete/DeleteCollection panics on unset mock expectations, crashing the test binary non-deterministically

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete` and `DeleteCollection`, after a successful storage operation the code unconditionally starts a goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.Delete(...)` / `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)` (see `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Delete(...) ... }()` and similar for delete-collection). In `dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, `TestMode3_Delete` and `TestMode3_DeleteCollection` only set expectations on the storage mock (`m.On("Delete"...)` / `m.On("DeleteCollection"...)`) and do not set any expectations for the legacy calls, yet they construct `ls := legacyStoreMock{m, l}` sharing the same `*mock.Mock`. With testify/mock, an unexpected method call typically triggers a panic, and because it happens in an async goroutine, it can crash the test process in a timing-dependent way (potentially after the test has already returned).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestMode3_Create error case mocks only legacy storage (setupStorageFn is nil) but Create calls Storage.Create first, so the error path doesn't exercise the intended failure

adjudication.rationale: In `TestMode3_Create`, the "error when creating object in the unified store fails" case sets only `setupLegacyFn` (expects `LegacyStorage.Create` to error) and leaves `setupStorageFn` nil. But `DualWriterMode3.Create` calls `d.Storage.Create(...)` first and returns early on error, never calling legacy in that path. As written, the test won’t exercise “unified store create fails”; instead it will hit an unmocked `Storage.Create` call (via the shared `mock.Mock`), likely causing a test failure or at minimum not testing the intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mode 3 tests lack AssertExpectations and legacy-call-count assertions, so nothing verifies the async legacy write (the core dual-write contract) actually happens

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, the new Mode 3 tests set up testify mock expectations via `m.On(...)` (including legacy `Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection`), but none of the tests call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` (or otherwise assert call counts) to verify those expectations were met. Since Mode 3 now performs legacy writes asynchronously via `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.*(...) }()`, the tests can pass without ever proving the async legacy write occurred (or occurred before the test ends). Thus the core dual-write contract isn’t actually validated by these tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update now passes raw objInfo to legacy instead of the updateWrapper with the storage-returned object, so legacy may persist different content/resourceVersion than unified storage, with no test covering this divergence

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Update was changed from wrapping objInfo in an updateWrapper that pins the legacy write to the storage-returned object, to calling legacy with the original objInfo: `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` inside the goroutine. This can allow legacy to compute a different updated object/resourceVersion than unified storage, reintroducing divergence. The new tests in dualwriter_mode3_test.go mock Update with `mock.Anything` for objInfo and do not assert that legacy receives the storage-returned object, so this divergence isn’t covered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Async legacy writes derive from the request ctx which may be cancelled when the handler returns; no test covers context cancellation, the 10s timeout path, or swallowed legacy-write errors

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy operations are now launched in goroutines and use `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)` where `ctx` is the request-scoped context passed into the handler (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`). This means the async legacy writes are cancelled if the parent `ctx` is cancelled, and legacy errors are effectively ignored (no `log.Error` in the goroutine; only `recordLegacyDuration(...)`/metrics are called). The new tests in `dualwriter_mode3_test.go` also don’t cover context cancellation or the 10s timeout path, and they don’t assert legacy-write behavior (no waiting for goroutines / no `AssertExpectations`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern about observability/semantics and test coverage, though whether request-context cancellation actually happens on handler return isn’t provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metrics are misattributed: Create/Update error paths record storage duration as legacy metric, and DeleteCollection async legacy path calls recordStorageDuration for the legacy call; no metrics-assertion test exists

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows misattributed metric recording in several paths: in DualWriterMode3.Create, the storage error path calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage) instead of a storage metric; in DualWriterMode3.Update, the storage error path similarly calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage); and in DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection, the async legacy goroutine calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy) even though it is timing the legacy call. The added tests in dualwriter_mode3_test.go do not assert any metrics behavior, supporting the finding’s “no metrics-assertion test exists” point.

adjudication_records.issue_text: wantErr test cases only assert.Error and return early without asserting which store produced the error or calling AssertExpectations, so error paths may pass for spurious reasons

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added Mode3 tests (e.g., TestMode3_Create/Get/List/Delete/DeleteCollection/Update), the `wantErr` branches do only `assert.Error(t, err)` and `return` without checking mock call expectations (no `m.AssertExpectations(t)` or call-count assertions) or verifying the error originated from the intended store (storage vs legacy). As written, an error could satisfy the test even if it comes from an unexpected call/order, leaving error-path behavior under-specified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestMode3_Delete error case returns before async legacy goroutine can run, risking cross-test contamination via the now-shared package-level prometheus registry (mode1 test removed its local registry), which can panic on duplicate metric registration

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, the legacy async goroutine is only started after a successful `d.Storage.Delete`. On the error path (`if err != nil { ... return ... }`) it returns immediately and does **not** launch any goroutine, so the finding’s premise (“error case returns before async legacy goroutine can run”) is not supported by the diff. Also, any duplicate Prometheus registration panic would stem from constructing `NewDualWriter(..., p)` multiple times against the same registry (constructor-time), not from the legacy goroutine in `Delete`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent fire-and-forget divergence from legacy storage: legacy writes converted to untracked goroutines with 10s timeout; failures cause permanent divergence with no retry, queue, or error surfacing beyond a metric (dualwriter_mode3.go Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection)

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy mutations were changed from synchronous best-effort calls to fire-and-forget goroutines using `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...)` where `ctx` is the request context (Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection). Because the parent `ctx` is likely canceled as soon as the handler returns, these async legacy calls can be canceled immediately and never execute/complete, causing real divergence from legacy storage. Additionally, failures in these goroutines are not surfaced to the caller and mostly aren’t even logged (only durations recorded), so divergence can occur silently with no retry/queue mechanism shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update no longer propagates the unified-store result to legacy: objInfo is passed raw to d.Legacy.Update so legacy re-derives from its own stale state; updateWrapper may now be dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the previous logic fetched the object from unified storage, computed the updated object once, and then used an `updateWrapper` so both `Storage.Update` and `Legacy.Update` would apply the same already-materialized updated object (including passing the unified-store result into the legacy call). The new implementation directly calls `d.Storage.Update(...)` and then asynchronously calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the original `objInfo` (no wrapper, no propagation of the unified-store result). That means the legacy update can re-run `UpdatedObject` against legacy’s own current object state (potentially stale/divergent), producing a different update than what was written to unified storage. This matches the finding and also implies the removed `updateWrapper` behavior is no longer present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Data race: obj, options, listOptions, and request-scoped ctx are handed to background goroutines while the handler continues; storage layers mutate passed objects

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, Mode3 now performs legacy writes asynchronously via `go func()` in `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, and `DeleteCollection`, closing over request-scoped inputs like `ctx`, `obj`/`objInfo`, `options`, and `listOptions` (e.g., `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...); ... d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ..., options) }()`). The diff does not prove that any of these values are mutated concurrently (so an actual data race is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone), but it is a concrete diff-grounded concern: using the same request context and pointer arguments in background goroutines can lead to subtle concurrency/cancellation issues if callers or storage implementations mutate/reuse those objects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete regression: NotFound from unified store aborts and skips legacy delete, though old code tolerated NotFound and still deleted from legacy

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, the old Delete logic explicitly tolerated NotFound from d.Storage.Delete (only returning on errors that were not NotFound) and still proceeded to call d.Legacy.Delete. The new Delete implementation returns immediately on any storage error (including NotFound): `if err != nil { ... return res, async, err }`, so legacy delete is skipped when unified store reports NotFound, matching the described regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric calls record the wrong backend: Create/Update error paths call recordLegacyDuration on storage failures; DeleteCollection goroutine calls recordStorageDuration for a legacy operation

adjudication.rationale:
In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, the metrics functions are wired to the wrong backend in several places:
- `Create`: on `d.Storage.Create` failure it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` even though the failed operation was storage (`startStorage` is the storage timer).
- `Update`: on `d.Storage.Update` failure it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` again attributing a storage failure to legacy.
- `DeleteCollection`: the goroutine performing `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)` records via `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`, misattributing a legacy operation to storage.
These are concrete, verifiable mis-recordings introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete success metric passes name in the kind label slot, creating unbounded label cardinality and polluting per-kind aggregation

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, the success-path metric call uses `name` in the third argument where other paths pass `options.Kind`: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. This will put the object name into the label slot intended for kind (or an equivalent low-cardinality dimension), causing unbounded label cardinality and breaking per-kind aggregation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplication: legacy-goroutine boilerplate is copy-pasted 4x in Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection; should be extracted into a helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nearly identical goroutine+timeout boilerplate for legacy writes in Mode3 across multiple methods: Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection each spin up `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(...); defer cancel(); ... d.Legacy.<Op>(...); d.recordLegacyDuration(...) }()`. This is a concrete maintainability/consistency concern introduced by the change (not a functional defect), and extracting a helper could reduce copy/paste and prevent future divergence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete builds a detailed log with WithValues but discards it, using d.Log in klog.NewContext instead; error branch logs without name/kind

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, the code builds a contextual logger (`log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`) but then sets the context with `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`, discarding those values for any downstream `klog.FromContext` logging inside `Storage.Delete` / `Legacy.Delete` and the goroutine. However, the immediate `log.Error(...)` calls in this function still include `name/kind/method`, so the finding’s claim about the local error branch logging without them is not strictly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests are racy/nondeterministic against new async writes: tests assert immediately without waiting for goroutines, and unified-store failure test cases stub only legacy so unstubbed storage calls panic on mock.Mock

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes Mode3 legacy writes asynchronous (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection spawn goroutines calling d.Legacy.*). However, multiple new tests in pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go do not stub the legacy calls that will occur asynchronously, which will trigger testify/mock unexpected-call panics (e.g., TestMode3_Delete and TestMode3_DeleteCollection only set Storage expectations, but Mode3 always calls Legacy.Delete/Legacy.DeleteCollection in a goroutine on success). Additionally, the Mode3 Create failure test case stubs only Legacy.Create while the implementation calls Storage.Create first and returns on its error, so the Storage call is unstubbed and will also panic on mock.Mock.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test assertions are tautological: repeated assert.NotEqual(t, obj, anotherObj) lines assert nothing, and TestMode3_Create checks a fixture property (GetResourceVersion()=="1") not behavior

adjudication.rationale: The new Mode3 tests repeatedly do `assert.NotEqual(t, obj, anotherObj)` immediately after (or instead of) asserting `obj == exampleObj` (e.g., in `TestMode3_Get`, `TestMode3_List`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_Update`). When `exampleObj` and `anotherObj` are distinct fixtures, the `NotEqual` adds little or nothing beyond the equality assertion. In `TestMode3_Create`, the main check is `GetResourceVersion() == "1"`, which appears to validate a property of the returned fixture rather than specifically validating DualWriter Mode3 behavior (e.g., that storage create is used and legacy is invoked asynchronously). This is a concrete test-quality issue but not a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Create returns (created, err) after err was checked nil; misleading and will break silently if the guard above is edited

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, `err` is checked immediately after `d.Storage.Create(...)` and the function returns early on error. On the success path, `err` is necessarily `nil`, so `return created, err` is equivalent to `return created, nil` and does not introduce a verifiable defect in this diff. The claim that it "will break silently if the guard above is edited" is speculative and not something that can be validated from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mode 1 test change removes local prometheus registry and depends on shared package-level p, creating hidden cross-test coupling and potential registration races in concurrent subtests

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode1_test.go`, the local `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` was removed but `NewDualWriter(Mode1, ls, us, p)` still passes `p`, implying it now relies on some shared/package-level `p` defined elsewhere. That creates hidden coupling between tests via a shared Prometheus registry and can lead to metric registration conflicts/flakiness if multiple tests construct dual writers against the same registry (especially if tests/subtests are run in parallel), even though the diff alone doesn’t prove an actual race occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mode 3 semantics changed from synchronous legacy sync to best-effort divergent background sync with no reconciliation mechanism; needs an explicit divergence-handling strategy (retry queue, backfill job)

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, Mode 3 write paths (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) were changed to perform the LegacyStorage operation asynchronously in a goroutine with a 10s timeout (`go func(){ ... d.Legacy.<op>(...) }()`), whereas previously Legacy writes/deletes were attempted synchronously before returning. Errors from the legacy operation are now only recorded via metrics and not surfaced or retried, and there is no reconciliation/backfill mechanism shown in the diff. This is a real, diff-grounded change in consistency/semantics (best-effort background sync) that warrants an explicit divergence-handling strategy, but it’s not a directly verifiable correctness defect given Mode 3 reads from Storage and legacy failures were previously ignored anyway.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy write goroutines in dualwriter_mode3.go use the incoming request context as parent, which is cancelled when the handler returns, so legacy writes are typically aborted immediately and the legacy store diverges; goroutines must use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a background context

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy writes are moved into goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) and each goroutine derives its context from the incoming request ctx via context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...). Since request contexts are typically canceled when the handler returns, these derived contexts will also be canceled immediately after returning from the storage call, causing the async legacy operations to abort and potentially diverge legacy vs unified storage. No context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or background context is used to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete regresses NotFound handling: new code returns early on any unified storage error, so legacy-only objects (created before mode 3) fail to delete from unified and their legacy copy is orphaned forever; same pattern in DeleteCollection

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Delete now returns immediately on any Storage.Delete error (`if err != nil { ... return res, async, err }`), so a NotFound from unified storage will skip the legacy delete goroutine entirely. Previously, NotFound was explicitly tolerated (via apierrors.IsNotFound) so legacy deletion still ran. The same early-return pattern exists in DeleteCollection: it now returns on any Storage.DeleteCollection error and never attempts legacy deletion, whereas the prior code always attempted legacy delete even if storage errored. This can orphan legacy-only objects/collections created before mode 3.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update's legacy goroutine passes the original objInfo to d.Legacy.Update, re-deriving the object from legacy's old state with non-deterministic UpdatedObject, causing the two stores to store different objects; also silently errors if legacy has no object and forceAllowCreate is false

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the legacy write goroutine now calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the original `objInfo` (see new goroutine), whereas the previous implementation computed the updated object once (based on Storage’s old state) and wrapped `objInfo` (`updateWrapper{updated: ...}`) so Legacy would persist the same updated object. With the new code, Legacy will re-run `UpdatedObject` against Legacy’s own old object state, which can differ from Storage’s, potentially producing different stored objects. Additionally, the goroutine ignores any legacy error beyond metrics (no log/propagation), so failures like a missing legacy object when `forceAllowCreate` is false will be silent to the caller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Shared runtime.Object is used concurrently by unified Storage.Create (which mutates it with resourceVersion/UID/timestamps), the client response serialization, and the legacy goroutine, creating a data race

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, after `d.Storage.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` returns, the code launches a goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` using the same `obj` reference that was passed into (and likely returned from) the unified storage call. If unified storage returns/uses the same underlying object (a common pattern with `runtime.Object` in apiserver storage paths), the caller may concurrently read/serialize the returned object while the legacy goroutine is also operating on it, creating a potential data race. The diff introduces this new concurrent legacy write without copying `obj`/`created`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete success path records the user-controlled object name as a metric label instead of options.Kind, causing unbounded Prometheus label cardinality / registry bloat

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go Delete(), the success path calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) using the object `name` (user-controlled, high-cardinality) where other paths use `options.Kind` (e.g., error path uses options.Kind). If that argument is used as a Prometheus label (as implied by the finding), it would cause unbounded label cardinality / registry bloat.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Misattributed metrics: Create storage-error path calls recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration; Update storage-error path has the same swap; DeleteCollection legacy goroutine calls recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows incorrect metrics functions being called on specific paths in pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go: (1) Create(): on Storage.Create error it calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage) instead of recordStorageDuration. (2) Update(): on Storage.Update error it likewise calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage) instead of recordStorageDuration. (3) DeleteCollection(): in the goroutine that calls d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, it records via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy) instead of recordLegacyDuration. These are verifiable swaps introduced by the diff and would misattribute metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy goroutine errors are silently swallowed with no retry, log, or count; error logging present in old code was removed in this diff, leaving no mechanism to detect or repair legacy misses

adjudication.rationale: In `dualwriter_mode3.go`, legacy writes/deletes/updates were changed from synchronous calls with explicit error logging to fire-and-forget goroutines (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`). Inside these goroutines, legacy errors are not logged or returned; they are only passed to `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...)` (and in one case `DeleteCollection` even calls `recordStorageDuration` in the legacy goroutine). So error visibility via logs was removed, which is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/regression concern. However, the finding overstates that there is "no ... count" because the diff does add metric recording with an error boolean, which can detect failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete builds a structured log with name/kind/method values but passes the base d.Log to klog.NewContext, so goroutine calls lose the structured log fields
matched_golden_ids: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate notes that Delete creates a structured logger with name/kind/method but mistakenly uses the base d.Log when creating the context via klog.NewContext, causing those fields not to propagate—same issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests in dualwriter_mode3_test.go reference an undefined registry variable p (only declared in TestMode3_Get), so tests don't compile unless p is a package-level var elsewhere; also TestMode3_Update's async failure-path goroutine makes mock expectations non-deterministic

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go, several tests call NewDualWriter(..., p) but do not define p in their scope (e.g., TestMode3_Create/List/Delete/DeleteCollection/Update). Only TestMode3_Get declares `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()`. Based on the diff alone, this would fail to compile unless there is a package-level `p` defined in some other file (not shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests never assert LegacyStorage.Create/Update/Delete were invoked, so mode 3's core dual-write contract is untested and tests pass even if legacy writes never happen

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, the new Mode3 tests set up legacy expectations via `m.On("Create"/"Update"/"Delete"...)`, but they never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` / `AssertCalled` / `AssertNumberOfCalls` (nor use `.Once()` with an assertion), so the tests will still pass even if the legacy methods are never invoked. This is especially relevant because the Mode3 implementation now performs legacy writes asynchronously in goroutines (e.g., `Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection` in `dualwriter_mode3.go`), making it easy for tests to miss validating the dual-write contract without explicit synchronization and assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: List/Get metrics use options.Kind as a label, but TypeMeta on options is typically empty from real clients, making the kind dimension near-always empty and useless for per-resource failure analysis

adjudication.rationale: In DualWriterMode3, Get/List (and other methods) attach/record labels using `options.Kind` (e.g., `Get`: `log := d.Log.WithValues("kind", options.Kind, ...)` and `d.recordStorageDuration(..., options.Kind, ...)`; `List`: same with `options.Kind`). The diff itself shows callers often pass options structs without TypeMeta populated (e.g., tests call `dw.Get(..., &metav1.GetOptions{})`, which yields empty `Kind`), so the resulting metric/log dimension can frequently be empty, reducing per-resource observability. This is a metrics/diagnostics design concern rather than a functional defect.
